title: dnsmasq: DS record log buffer overflow
ai_system: Revelio using Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.6
organization: UC Berkeley Revelio research team and affected project maintainers
summary: The Revelio paper identifies a heap-based buffer overflow in dnsmasq v2.93test9: ds record log buffer overflow. It lists the author-assessed severity as High and says the finding was manually validated with a reproducible sanitizer-backed proof of vulnerability through a reachable project test harness. This is Table V item 1 of the seven-project real-world hunt.
ai_role: The paper describes Revelio as using Claude Haiku 4.5 for hypothesis generation and Claude Sonnet 4.6 for proof-of-vulnerability confirmation; its experimental-method section says this configuration was used for the seven-project OSS-Fuzz hunt. The authors state all 19 tabled findings were manually validated and sanitizer-confirmed. The paper does not provide a per-item model trajectory, so the exact division of Claude work within this row is not independently stated.
classification_note: The paper publicly identifies this distinct finding on 2026-06-20. The authors describe the hunt as searching for previously unknown flaws, but this record does not assert exploitation in the wild or operational zero-day status.
remediation_note: Red Hat’s CVE record describes the bounded logging-path overflow and points to upstream fix commit 36d081e37477027fd721fea498f3760f529034ad; disabling query logging is a mitigation when DNSSEC remains enabled.

impacts.conditions: dnsmasq has both DNSSEC validation and query logging enabled; an attacker supplies DNS replies with unsupported algorithm or digest types that overflow the logging buffer.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.
